A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same study, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and complete Appendices A–D. The extensive reformatting does not prevent reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original LLM training experiments, validation losses, downstream evaluations, sensitivity analyses, and scaling-law fits in the main text and Appendix C.

after.justification: v2 retains these original empirical results, including the schedule comparisons in Table 1, downstream evaluations in Table 5, and experiments throughout Appendix C.

M1.justification: The warmup and linear decay-to-zero procedure, AdamW and µP setup, and Rational schedule in Appendix D.1 remain unchanged. No algorithmic or architectural component is added or revised.

E1.justification: Both versions use SlimPajama, OpenWebText, the English/Arabic/source-code mixture for scaling experiments, and the same downstream tasks in Table 5. No dataset, task, or evaluation scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Table 1 retains the same InvSqrt, Constant, cosine, and linear schedule comparisons. Figure 8 retains Cyclic and WSD, and comparator participation in the appendix experiments is unchanged.

E3.justification: Training budgets, model configurations, learning-rate sweeps, batch-size protocols, 10% warmup, and evaluation procedures remain unchanged. Tables 2, 3, and 6 contain identical settings, and validation still uses 1.1B held-out tokens.

E4.justification: The analyses of training duration, batch size, weight decay, sparsity, step decay, recency overfitting, NanoGPT numerical precision, and scaling behavior are retained. No ablation or supplementary analysis is added or substantively revised.

E5.justification: Appendix C.9 and Figure 24 report the same five runs with different random seeds and mean validation losses with standard-deviation error bars. The shared-seed policy for the main comparisons is also unchanged.

E6.justification: All six tables have identical contents, and the plotted results are unchanged. For example, Table 1 retains best Linear-D2Z and Linear-10× losses of 2.571 and 2.591, respectively; Table 5 and Figure 26 retain the same downstream results and scaling fits.

T1.justification: Equations (1)–(8), the initial-coefficient derivation in Appendix B.1, and the Rational schedule derivation in Appendix D.1 are mathematically unchanged. Differences concern typesetting and placement.

C1.justification: Both versions retain the claims of Linear-D2Z superiority at compute-optimal training, increasing benefits at higher tokens-per-parameter, and 60% compute savings in the 610M-model example. The asserted contributions are unchanged.

C2.justification: The EMA and bias–variance interpretations, discussion of schedule dependence, and limitations concerning limited data, unstable high-learning-rate training, and other optimizers remain intact. Local wording edits do not introduce substantive explanations or qualifications.

D1.justification: v2 adds the Cerebras CS-3 hardware statement to the abstract, but v1 already disclosed this in Appendix A, together with training time. Implementation details, hyperparameters, hardware information, and code/data access information otherwise remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and positioning relative to learning-rate scheduling, µP, and AdamW averaging are unchanged. Some bibliography author lists are shortened to 'et al.', without adding or removing cited works.

P1.justification: v2 makes limited copyedits, changes title and heading capitalization, and repeats the hardware disclosure in the abstract. Sections 1–7 and Appendices A–D retain their narrative sequence without substantial rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 replaces the conference template with a Cerebras-branded design, changing typography, text width, headers, footers, caption styling, and finding boxes throughout. Existing figures and tables are resized and extensively repositioned, while their scientific contents remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: The result tables, experimental analyses, derivations, limitations, and reproducibility information remain unchanged. The extensive visual redesign leaves both versions readable, while the limited copyediting and repeated hardware disclosure do not resolve a substantive deficiency. Overall paper quality is materially unchanged.
